Before drafting, here's what I found and how I'll proceed.

**There is no implemented system yet.** The four workspace packages are untouched `uv init` stubs: a `hello()` function, empty READMEs, no dependencies and no tests. The root `sec-edgar` script points at a module that doesn't exist. The only substantive artifacts are `specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md` (status PROPOSED, 2026-10-05) and its ADR.

So the description can only cover the **proposed design** in that spec. The external critique will be a pre-implementation review of the design, not a review of how built code behaves. I'll say so in the document so the reviewer doesn't think the method has run.

**Granularity: system.** The components compose, so I'll use the system template. Components are named by role:

| Role | Output |
|---|---|
| Source-discovery process | Set of available source identities per period, with a coverage frontier |
| Budgeted collection process | Accepted, content-addressed snapshots under a single shared request budget |
| Parsing and normalization map | Per-snapshot observation sets under a parser/schema version |
| Identity and precedence resolution | Canonical record set per quarter from open/closed-quarter and daily observations |
| Reconciliation and withdrawal gate | Change set (additions, updates, withdrawals) and gated vs. automatic acceptance |
| Versioned publication | Per-quarter generations behind one conditionally updated pointer |

The core is the formal part: identity keys, precedence ordering, monotonicity of the open quarter, hash-bound withdrawal approval, and per-quarter atomicity. I'll write it as set-valued maps over observations rather than as Azure services. Azure products, CLI commands, config keys and field names become role-names or symbols in the notation table.

**One caveat on fit.** This skill is built for estimation and inference methods, and an ingestion pipeline has no likelihood or prior. The template slots still apply: the estimand is the true SEC filing-index membership and field values per quarter, observed through noisy, revisable, partially available snapshots. That framing gives the reviewer something real to push on, such as when absence is evidence of withdrawal.

If what you actually want is a review of the spec's trade-offs, the design-architecture skill fits more directly. Tell me if you'd rather go that way. Otherwise I'm proceeding.

Next steps:

```bash
echo "${LLM_WIKI_ROOT:-unset}"          # wiki pre-flight if set
cat specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md
```

After that I'll write `specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-methodology.md`, self-check it, run `check_decoupling.py` on it, and commit it before handing off.
